fields.overview_why_3_story: We adopt RMS, PMS, and collaboration tools GMs actually use—training tied to incentives, not shelf-ware. Owners see adoption metrics because software that does not stick becomes hidden labor cost and bad forecasts.
fields.energyEfficiency: Chiller optimization; guest-room occupancy-based HVAC in new builds.
fields.crisisExperience: Hurricanes; pandemic border rules; fuel and ferry disruptions for Cozumel transfers.
fields.overview_bestat_3_story: Weddings, incentives, and group accounts are staffed by experienced leaders—not interns with spreadsheets. Accounts have coverage plans for PTO and turnover; relationships survive system changes because continuity is designed. Owners see pipeline health weekly, not as a quarterly mystery.
fields.insuranceCoverage: Catastrophe and BI reviewed pre-season; deductibles in owner packs.
fields.brand_narrative_relationship: Franchise conversations include owners when rate floors, PIPs, or distribution changes affect cash. For independents, we document positioning and capex decision rights before conflict—capital partners see governance. We lead with options and data when brand and economics tension appears.
fields.managementPhilosophy: Revenue discipline without killing the guest experience: we guard ADR and GOP with the same rigor we guard guest safety and brand scores. If a promo buys share today at the expense of service tomorrow, we say no with numbers. GMs own both P&L and reviews—commercial is not a silo that outruns operations.
fields.overview_bestat_1_story: Riviera leisure cannot be planned on peak-month BAR alone—we model shoulders with real tour-operator commitments, wedding pipeline, and corporate transient in Mérida and Cancún as distinct curves. Owners see base, upside, and downside before budgets lock; we revisit when airlift, fuel, or border rules move. The point is credibility: owners and lenders should recognize the same demand story operations uses to schedule labor.
fields.missionStatement: Operate honestly in markets that change with the weather—literally.
fields.wasteReduction: Waste audits at high-F&B assets; plastic reduction aligned with coastal municipality programs; organic diversion where haulers exist—targets in annual ESG letter to owners.
fields.brand_soft_independent_narrative: Cenote Azul Operadores can help if you are evaluating soft-brand affiliation, an independent-to-branded conversion, or repositioning an independent resort, you can expect help interpreting brand requirements, protecting local identity, preparing operationally for a flag transition, and understanding how distribution and loyalty may affect your operating model.
fields.differentiators: Bilingual crisis communications with owner-approved templates; sargassum-season marketing pivots with pre-built inland and urban shoulder strategies; deep relationships with regional OTAs, wedding planners, and corporate accounts so channel mix is relationship-led, not only algorithm-led. We connect Riviera leisure math to Mérida corporate pace in one operating system—no fantasy BAR that collapses on Tuesday mornings.
fields.companyDescription: We started with two boutique hotels in Mérida and ended up running branded select-service along the Cancún–Tulum corridor. Owners like that we understand both tour-package pace and Monday corporate in Mérida. We are CALA-heavy with a small US border pipeline we do not oversell.
fields.brand_narrative_compliance: Brand QA includes beach safety, backup power tests, and pool chemistry on the same calendar as guest-facing standards—because in our corridor compliance is life-safety and brand equity together. Findings route to remediation owners can track; exceptions carry economic analysis.

fields.outcome: We rebuilt shoulder-season pricing with minimum LOS and packaging that matched actual staffing—no rate dumps that operations could not deliver—and flexed labor to a 22% reduction in paid hours per occupied room on low weeks without service-score collapse. F&B was simplified to margin-positive dayparts only. Shoulder-month GOP swung from negative to a consistent 18–22% of revenue within two full low seasons (about fourteen months); peak ADR held within 4% of prior highs.

We renegotiated tour-operator allotments with release windows and deposit terms that protected BAR on retail, then rebalanced OTA versus direct with parity monitoring and a simple member-direct perk. Net ADR after channel cost rose even when gross BAR looked flat. Occupancy index versus STR competitive set improved 6 points in eight months; distribution cost as a percent of rooms revenue fell 140 bps year over year.

We layered a corporate transient strategy on top of RMS guardrails—BAR floors, length-of-stay rules, and promo approvals logged with expected GOP trade—then staffed sales to match real pipeline, not slide promises. Group and corporate pace reviews moved to weekly with finance in the room. RevPAR finished +12% year over year with GOP margin up 190 basis points in the same period; the owner cleared incentive fee in month ten versus month fourteen under the prior regime.

We reset all-inclusive and à la carte menus to margin-first recipes, retrained service for faster table turns, and aligned beach F&B hours to actual demand curves—recovering $340K annualized in F&B profit in the first full year. Rooms used dynamic BAR with comp-aware floors. ADR recovered to 103% of 2019 same-month levels four months ahead of the bank’s model; RevPAR led the owner-selected comp strip by 7–11% for five straight months post-stabilization.
